articles.summary: Festival acontece nos dias 4, 5, 6, 7 e 11, 12 e 13 de setembro. Ingressos para dias de Calvin Harris e Maroon 5 já estão esgotados.
articles.body:
O Rock in Rio 2026 anunciou os horários de cada show do evento. ( Veja lista mais abaixo )

A programação está disponível no aplicativo do festival, que ainda traz informações e disponibilidades de serviços como reserva de lockers e compra de opções de transporte, como o Primeira Classe e o BRT Expresso Rock in Rio.

O Primeira Classe oferece um serviço exclusivo, com embarques em diversos pontos do Rio de Janeiro e da Grande Rio, além de atender fãs de cidades dos estados de São Paulo e Minas Gerais, deixando o público dentro da Cidade do Rock.

Já o BRT contará com três serviços especiais que farão ligações diretas e semidiretas até a Cidade do Rock, por meio dos corredores exclusivos do sistema para garantir viagens mais rápidas e confortáveis. Os serviços serão operados com ônibus articulados.

A partir do dia 4 de setembro, data de estreia do evento, o público também vai poder consultar através do aplicativo o mapa completo da Cidade do Rock e informações sobre as ativações das marcas parceiras, além dos horários das experiências do festival.

O Rock in Rio 2026 acontece no Parque Olímpico, no Rio de Janeiro, nos dias 4, 5, 6, 7 e 11, 12 e 13 de setembro.

Calvin Harris, Black Eyed Peas, Foo Fighters, Elton John e Maroon 5 são algumas das estrelas que se apresentam no festival.

O Rock in Rio 2026 será transmitido ao vivo nos dias 4, 5, 6, 7, 11, 12 e 13 de setembro, a partir das 15h15, pelo Multishow, e a partir das 15h50, pelo Canal Bis, e para assinantes do plano Premium do Globoplay, que também terão acesso à transmissão do Multishow em 4K, por meio de um sinal extra.

Quem não é assinante, também poderá acompanhar os cinco palcos do Rock in Rio pelo sinal aberto, que irá se revezar entre Multishow e Bis a cada 30 minutos, a partir das 15h30.

A TV Globo exibe flashes durante a programação e um especial todas as noites - às sextas (4 e 11/9), após o "Globo Repórter"; aos sábados (5 e 12/9), após o "Altas Horas"; aos domingos (6 e 13/9), após o "Boletim Estrelas da Casa", e na segunda (7/9), após o "Jornal da Globo".

articles.title: Como chegar no Rock in Rio de ônibus, carro ou metrô | G1
articles.standfirst: Melhor jeito de ir até a Cidade do Rock é de ônibus, mas outras alternativas são possíveis; veja detalhes sobre o trajeto.
articles.summary: Melhor jeito de ir até a Cidade do Rock é de ônibus, mas outras alternativas são possíveis; veja detalhes sobre o trajeto.
articles.body:
A 10ª edição do Rock in Rio começa no dia 4 de setembro. Serão sete dias de shows na Cidade do Rock, na Zona Oeste do Rio.

O festival está montado no Parque Olímpico da Barra , na Avenida Embaixador Abelardo Bueno. O melhor jeito de chegar é de ônibus . Há duas modalidades: o BRT Expresso Rock in Rio e o Primeira Classe .

O BRT Expresso Rock in Rio custa R$ 29 a ida e volta e terá três linhas especiais.

Já o Primeira Classe sai de diferentes pontos do RJ com destino a um terminal dentro da Cidade do Rock.

O bilhete do BRT especial custa R$ 29 e inclui ida e volta. A compra é feita exclusivamente pelo aplicativo Jaé , usando o saldo da Conta Transporte, que pode ser carregado por Pix ou cartão de crédito.

Cada pessoa poderá comprar até dez bilhetes por dia de festival.

SE008: Terminal Jardim Oceânico ↔ Terminal Centro Olímpico, sem paradas;

SE009: Terminal Alvorada ↔ Estação Morro do Outeiro, sem paradas;

SE010: Terminal Paulo da Portela ↔ Estação Morro do Outeiro, com paradas na Praça Seca, Tanque e Taquara.

O QR Code para embarque ficará disponível no Jaé uma semana antes do evento e só poderá ser utilizado no dia escolhido na compra. As gratuidades do sistema Jaé não valerão no BRT Expresso.

Na chegada, o passageiro receberá uma pulseira individual , necessária para utilizar o transporte especial na volta.

O bilhete custa R$ 220, ida e volta , e deixa dentro da Cidade do Rock, perto do palco New Dance Order.

Para a ida, o passageiro escolhe previamente seu ponto de embarque e o horário de saída, com partidas entre 11h e 19h.

Na volta, quem utiliza as rotas do Rio e da Região Metropolitana conta com mais flexibilidade: não é necessário agendar horário, e os ônibus começam a sair a partir das 22h, mediante demanda, com os últimos embarques acontecendo até duas horas após o término do Palco Mundo.

São 20 pontos de embarque no Rio e na Região Metropolitana, além de mais de 18 pontos fora da capital.

No Rio, há saídas de locais como Copacabana, Ipanema, Botafogo, Lagoa, Tijuca, Barra da Tijuca, Recreio, Galeão e diferentes shoppings. Também estão previstos embarques em cidades como São Paulo, Belo Horizonte, Petrópolis, Búzios, Cabo Frio, Campinas, Niterói, Nova Friburgo, Macaé e Volta Redonda.

A compra é feita pela internet , onde há os horários disponíveis.

Bloqueios de trânsito para o Rock in Rio — Foto: Reprodução

O festival recomenda pegar o transporte público e os ônibus especiais.

Ruas próximas à Cidade do Rock ficarão fechadas das 14h às 5h nos dias de shows, e somente moradores poderão passar pelos pontos de bloqueio — o cadastramento já se encerrou .

A Avenida Embaixador Abelardo Bueno , onde fica o portão da Cidade do Rock, por exemplo, estará totalmente interditada.

Vias internas, como a Aroazes , a Franz Weissman e a Francisco de Paula também serão fechadas.

Confira a lista completa de interdições:

Avenida Embaixador Abelardo Bueno, em toda a extensão;

Avenida Engenheiro Carlos Carvalho, entre a Estrada Coronel Pedro Corrêa e a Estrada Arroio Pavuna;

Estrada Coronel Pedro Corrêa, entre o retorno da estação BRT Pedro Corrêa e a Avenida Embaixador Abelardo Bueno;

Avenida Salvador Allende (pista lateral, sentido Estrada dos Bandeirantes), entre a passagem da pista lateral para a central, na altura da Rua Pedro Calmon, e o acesso da pista central para a lateral, próximo à estação BRT Morro do Outeiro;

Rua Francisco de Paula, entre a Avenida Embaixador Abelardo Bueno e a Avenida Jaime Poggi.

Sim — mas será necessário fazer baldeação . A Estação Jardim Oceânico, que faz a integração com o BRT especial, ficará aberta 24 horas para embarque.

As demais estações do sistema funcionarão em seu horário normal para embarque e, durante a madrugada, seguirão abertas, mas somente para desembarque.

A passagem custa R$ 7,90 por trecho. Quem fizer ida e volta usando metrô e BRT especial gastará R$ 44,80 no total.

A transferência entre as linhas 1 e 2 poderá ser feita no trecho entre Central do Brasil e Botafogo.

Primeira parte dos portões é aberta na Cidade do Rock. Fãs aguardam na grade para entrar no Rock in Rio.

A cidade do Rio de Janeiro entrou em Estágio 2 às 12h desta sexta-feira (4) em função do esquema operacional para o Rock in Rio e a mudança de rotina da cidade, com a antecipação no horário de saída em repartições públicas.

Em dia de sol forte, os fãs aguardam a abertura dos portões do Rock in Rio em uma fila, aproveitando a sombra de um poste.

Artistas que se apresentarão no palco Supernova fazem os últimos ensaios antes dos shows.

A Cidade do Rock está pronta para receber cerca de 100 mil fãs de música por dia. Confira as imagens do Parque Olímpico pronto para a abertura dos portões.

Roberta e Liz montaram uma espécie de barraca usando a estrutura de uma caçamba de lixo antes da abertura dos portões do Rock in Rio. As duas se conheceram em um grupo de mulheres criado para reunir fãs que vão juntas a shows. “Carioca, né? A gente tenta se proteger como pode. Ficar no sol, no osso, não dá” disse Liz.

Os fãs da banda Foo Fighters chegaram cedo aos portões da Cidade do Rock. Eles fizeram uma fila por ordem de chegada. Veja mais aqui.

O Palco Mundo, o principal do festival, contará com um telão de 2,4 mil metros quadrados para o vento. De acordo com Roberta Medina, vice-presidente da Rock World, o espaço vai ganhar a cara do artista que estiver se apresentando. Veja mais.

articles.title: Kai Trump reveals she's not 'eaten in 3 days' following major upheaval in personal life
articles.summary: Kai Trump documented her first week at the University of Miami with an emotional video shared to her YouTube – see details
articles.body:
President Donald Trump's granddaughter, Kai Trump, recently shared her emotional struggle with adjusting to college life at the University of Miami.

Kai documented her first week at college in a YouTube video, where she tearfully said goodbye to her family and friends before returning home due to illness.

The 19-year-old, who is a golf enthusiast, is one of five children of Vanessa and Donald Trump Jr., who divorced in 2018 but continue to co-parent their kids amicably.

President Donald Trump's granddaughter, Kai Trump , has opened up about struggling to adjust to college life as she began her first week at the University of Miami. The 19-year-old, who is in her freshman year, documented her experience in a new video shared on her YouTube channel.

In the vlog, Kai filmed herself driving home from the golf course the day she left her home in Jupiter, Florida, for school. "It's just really sad that I have to say goodbye to everyone today," she said with tears in her eyes.

"I'm not a very emotional person at all, so this is like really weird for me to cry, I've only cried a few times. I think knowing that I have to say goodbye to everyone tonight really, really sucks."

She continued: "I don't have to say goodbye to my mom tomorrow, but [saying goodbye to] everybody else [tonight] is sad. I'm struggling right now, just thinking about it." However, Kai added that she was "excited" for her next chapter but "emotional" about it.

Later in the video, Kai showed off her new Miami apartment and documented her first week attending golf practice and class. Kai's friend, Emma, visited her apartment and brought the teen lots of frozen food, as she shared that she "hadn't eaten in three days."

"It's all pre-cooked so she doesn't have to do anything crazy," said Emma. "She's living off of diet sodas, so I got her fruit and prosciutto and we got her some pasta and bread and stuff, like basic foods, she's basically living off of diet soda."

Kai's first week at college was cut short as she was forced to return home after suffering from Strep throat. "I got sick with Strep on Wednesday, my first week of school," she shared. "I came all the way back to Jupiter because I was so sick I needed my mom to nurse me back to health."

Kai is one out of five of Vanessa and Donald Trump Jr.'s children. The couple tied the knot back in 2005 and share Kai Madison, Donald Trump III, Tristan Milos, Spencer Frederick, and Chloe Sophia. The pair divorced in 2018, but continue to amicably co-parent their kids.

The teen is a golf enthusiast and has been playing the sport for over 13 years. "Golf has always been a massive part of my life and is my biggest passion. I always aspire to be a leader and a positive figure on and off the golf course," she previously shared.

articles.title: Evento gratuito em Sarapuí une esporte e história neste domingo | G1
articles.standfirst: Evento gratuito terá duas opções de trajeto pela zona rural do município. Os trajetos buscam unir esporte e turismo rural. Os ciclistas passarão por propriedades e cerca de 25 capelas históricas.
articles.summary: A 1ª Ciclorrota da Fé em Sarapuí oferece trajetos gratuitos de até 79 km por propriedades rurais e igrejas históricas, promovendo o turismo e o esporte na região.
articles.body:
A Prefeitura de Sarapuí (SP) promove, neste domingo (6), a 1ª edição da Ciclorrota da Fé com dois percursos pela zona rural do município: um de 23 quilômetros e outro de 79 quilômetros. As inscrições são gratuitas e devem ser feitas pelo site .

A proposta é unir esporte, turismo e cultura, permitindo que moradores e visitantes conheçam paisagens rurais, propriedades, áreas de mata e pontos históricos da cidade. A largada será às 8h30, em frente à Igreja Matriz Nossa Senhora das Dores.

Ao g1 , Marcio José Ricardo Sturaro, diretor municipal de Sarapuí, disse que os dois trajetos foram pensados para atender diferentes perfis de participantes.

"O percurso de 23 km é uma opção mais curta para quem está começando ou não está acostumado a percorrer longas distâncias. Já o percurso de 79 km oferece um desafio maior para quem busca uma experiência mais longa de ciclismo."

Além da diferença de distância, os caminhos também são distintos. O percurso mais longo passa por um número maior de bairros e pontos de interesse, incluindo capelas e igrejas históricas espalhadas pela zona rural.

"O passeio é uma oportunidade de apresentar Sarapuí por meio de seus caminhos rurais, sua história e seus espaços de importância cultural. Muitas das capelas e igrejas encontradas pelo trajeto têm mais de 100 anos e fazem parte da história das comunidades do município", explica Sturaro.

Capela São Roque, de 1932, em Sarapuí, é um dos pontos visitados durante o trajeto — Foto: Prefeitura de Sarapuí/Divulgação

Ao todo, cerca de 25 igrejas e capelas podem ser observadas ao longo dos percursos, embora a quantidade varie de acordo com o trajeto escolhido .

"Uma equipe acompanhará o percurso e auxiliará na orientação dos participantes. Algumas capelas estarão diretamente no caminho e poderão ser identificadas durante o trajeto. Já aquelas localizadas fora da rota principal serão indicadas, permitindo que cada participante decida se deseja fazer o desvio para conhecê-las", relata o diretor municipal.

Igrejas e capelas podem ser observadas ao longo dos percursos percorridos de bicicleta em Sarapuí (SP) — Foto: Prefeitura de Sarapuí/Divulgação

Além das construções religiosas, os ciclistas terão contato com diferentes características da vida rural de Sarapuí, como propriedades, animais, áreas de cultivo, casarões antigos e estabelecimentos existentes ao longo das estradas.

"O município está inserido predominantemente no bioma Mata Atlântica, com áreas de transição entre a Mata Atlântica e o Cerrado. Durante o trajeto, os participantes poderão observar áreas de mata, estradas rurais, regiões próximas a cursos d'água e outras paisagens naturais", detalha Maurício.

Evento de ciclismo em Sarapuí (SP) passará por propriedades rurais e construções religiosas — Foto: Prefeitura de Sarapuí/Divulgação

A prefeitura informou que uma equipe da administração municipal estará presente durante o percurso para orientar os participantes. O trajeto será sinalizado e contará com indicações dos principais pontos de interesse e locais de parada.

Todos os ciclistas receberão uma medalha ao final do percurso.

Os participantes também podem doar 1 litro de leite, que será arrecadado pela organização e encaminhado ao Fundo Social de Solidariedade de Sarapuí. Os donativos serão destinados a famílias que necessitam de assistência.

Segundo a prefeitura, a proposta surgiu a partir da ideia de utilizar o ciclismo como uma maneira de conhecer e valorizar diferentes regiões de Sarapuí, especialmente os caminhos e atrativos existentes na zona rural.

"Sarapuí faz parte da região turística Veredas da Mata Atlântica, que trabalha com a proposta de fortalecer o turismo regional e desenvolver roteiros que integrem os municípios da região. O percurso utiliza esses espaços como pontos de interesse, unindo a prática esportiva ao conhecimento da história e da cultura local", comenta o diretor municipal.

O evento não integra, ainda, um programa estadual específico. Segundo a prefeitura, a iniciativa foi criada pelo próprio município após a administração observar projetos semelhantes desenvolvidos por outras cidades da região turística.

Percurso mais longo passa por um número maior de bairros e pontos de interesse, incluindo capelas e igrejas históricas espalhadas pela zona rural de Sarapuí (SP) — Foto: Prefeitura de Sarapuí/Divulgação

De acordo com a prefeitura, o município vem adotando medidas para ampliar sua participação no cenário turístico regional e nacional.

Entre as ações estão a criação de uma estrutura específica para o turismo, com assessor da área, e a previsão de um cargo efetivo de tecnólogo em turismo, por meio de concurso público.

O município também encaminhou a documentação necessária para buscar o título de Município de Interesse Turístico (MIT) junto à Secretaria de Turismo e Viagens. Sarapuí também integra o Mapa do Turismo Brasileiro, do Ministério do Turismo.

Sarapuí tem quase um búfalo para cada dois moradores — Foto: Divulgação/Prefeitura de Sarapuí

Além da Ciclorrota, a administração mantém iniciativas como o projeto Pé na Roça, Boia Cross, Feira Livre, Feira da Lua e Festival do Búfalo.

"Também está sendo desenvolvido um trabalho de resgate do patrimônio histórico, com destaque para o casario colonial e a história relacionada ao tropeirismo. Outros levantamentos e ações de resgate histórico também estão sendo estudados, incluindo aspectos da história religiosa ligada a João de Camargo e a história das comunidades quilombolas e do caxambu no bairro dos Cocaes", concluiu o diretor municipal.

Município de Sarapuí (SP) realiza torneio de pesca — Foto: Divulgação/Prefeitura Municipal de Sarapuí

No Centro de Sarapuí, os três imóveis ficam a apenas 600 metros de distância um do outro. O primeiro, localizado na Rua Doutor Cerqueira César, foi construído por imigrantes alemães e tem cerca de 126 anos. O segundo, na Rua Doutor Luiz Vergueiro, existe há 111 anos e foi utilizado como casa paroquial. Já o terceiro, na Rua Quintino Bocaiúva, foi erguido há mais de 140 anos.

O casarão na região central de Sarapuí foi construído entre 1850 e 1870 — Foto: João Paulo Netto/Arquivo pessoal

O professor, pesquisador e arquiteto Igor Chaves, de Itapetininga (SP), explica que os casarões precisam ser preservados, estudados e registrados, principalmente para que as novas gerações possam conhecer e compreender melhor o passado da cidade.

"A preservação de prédios históricos é fundamental não apenas por seu valor arquitetônico ou estético, mas sobretudo por aquilo que representam: são testemunhos vivos da história, das memórias coletivas e das formas de vida que moldaram a identidade de nossa cidade", apontou.

articles.title: Di Ferrero no Rock in Rio: show une hits do NX Zero e fase solo | G1
articles.standfirst: Cantor abriu o Palco Sunset nesta sexta-feira (4) e recebeu Danilo Cutrim como convidado especial.
articles.summary: Di Ferrero abriu o Palco Sunset nesta sexta (4) com sucessos do NX Zero e músicas solo. O show contou com a participação especial de Danilo Cutrim.
articles.body:
Di Ferrero voltou ao palco do Rock in Rio nesta sexta-feira (4). O cantor tem uma relação antiga com o festival e já passou quatro vezes pela Cidade do Rock ao longo da carreira.

A estreia aconteceu em 2011, quando o NX Zero abriu os trabalhos do Palco Mundo. Onze anos depois, ele retornou ao evento para dividir o Palco Sunset com Vitor Kley. Em 2024, voltou ao festival ao lado dos antigos companheiros de banda, em um show no Sunset que marcou o encerramento da turnê de reencontro do NX Zero, realizada após uma pausa de seis anos.

O show desta sexta começou pontualmente às 15h30, com “Universo Paralelo”, e emendou com “Só Rezo”, animando os fãs do NX Zero logo no início da apresentação.

Nem o sol afastou o público, que atendeu a cada pedido do cantor e entoou, aos berros, os refrões dos sucessos. Bem perto do palco, uma fã mais do que especial acompanhava o show: Isabeli Fontana, mulher de Di Ferrero.

Di Ferrero canta no Rock in Rio 2026 — Foto: Reprodução/Globo

“É um sonho estar aqui sempre. Bem-vindos à turnê S7te”, disse o cantor antes de emendar com um cover de “Come as You Are”, do Nirvana. Para os românticos, Ferrero também apresentou uma versão de “Aonde Quer Que Eu Vá”, dos Paralamas do Sucesso.

Di Ferrero uniu passado e presente em seu repertório no Rock in Rio. Os clássicos do NX Zero apareceram em diferentes momentos da apresentação e dividiram espaço com canções de sua carreira solo.

O cantor ainda recebeu um convidado especial: Danilo Cutrim, vocalista das bandas Forfun e Braza. Juntos, eles apresentaram “História de Verão”, acompanhados em coro pelo público.

O setlist foi permeado por sucessos do NX Zero, como “Cedo ou Tarde”, “Daqui Pra Frente”, “Pela Última Vez”, “Cartas Pra Você”, “Além de Mim” e “Onde Estiver”, reforçando a conexão com o público que acompanhou a banda nos anos 2000.

Ao mesmo tempo, Di Ferrero apresentou músicas de seu trabalho mais recente, o álbum "S7te", incluindo “Deixa Sonhar”, mostrando ao público a nova fase de sua carreira.

O cantor encerrou com "Razões e Emoções" e "Onde estiver". Para o primeiro show do festival, Di Ferrero colocou o sarrafo bem alto para as próximas atrações.

articles.title: Perdeu seu filho na Cidade do Rock? Saiba o que fazer | G1
articles.standfirst: Responsáveis por menores de 16 anos podem registrar dados antes do festival e retirar pulseira de identificação nas entradas do evento.
articles.summary: Responsáveis por menores de 16 anos podem registrar dados antes do festival e retirar pulseira de identificação nas entradas do evento.
articles.body:
Quem for ao Rock in Rio com crianças e adolescentes de até 16 anos poderá cadastrá-los em um sistema de identificação disponibilizado pela organização do festival. Segundo o evento, o objetivo é agilizar a localização dos responsáveis em casos de desencontro dentro da Cidade do Rock.

O cadastro deve ser feito previamente pela internet pelo site . Depois, já no local, os responsáveis precisam procurar os pontos de identificação nas entradas do festival para retirar uma pulseira destinada ao menor .

Para concluir o processo, é necessário vincular ao cadastro o número impresso na pulseira . Com isso, equipes do festival poderão consultar os contatos de emergência informados pelos responsáveis caso a criança ou adolescente se perca.

Cadastro deve ser feito pelo site — Foto: Reprodução

A organização recomenda que o registro seja realizado antes da chegada ao evento para evitar filas e agilizar o acesso ao sistema de identificação.

O Rock in Rio 2026 será transmitido ao vivo pelo Globoplay , Multishow e Bis . Na Globo , haverá entradas durante a programação e um programa especial, ao fim de cada noite, com os melhores momentos do festival.

Nesta sexta, a Fundação para a Infância e Adolescência (FIA), por meio do programa SOS Crianças Desaparecidas, realiza uma mobilização de orientação, informação e prevenção ao desaparecimento de crianças e adolescentes na estação do metrô da Central do Brasil e na rodoviária do Rio.

Durante a mobilização, equipes distribuem materiais informativos, orientar pais, responsáveis e familiares sobre medidas preventivas e realizar a identificação de crianças e adolescentes.

A iniciativa busca ampliar a conscientização das famílias sobre cuidados simples que podem contribuir para evitar situações de desaparecimento em locais de grande movimentação.

Entre os principais cuidados a serem tomados, recomenda-se que pais e responsáveis mantenham a criança sempre próxima, evitem que ela circule sozinha em locais de grande aglomeração e utilizem mecanismos de identificação, como pulseiras ou etiquetas com dados de contato, durante o evento.

articles.title: Rock in Rio: Fotos da Cidade do Rock e do novo Palco Mundo | G1
articles.standfirst: Festival estreia novo Palco Mundo, com telão de mais de 2 mil metros quadrados, e promete mudanças visuais a cada apresentação.
articles.summary: O Rock in Rio estreia com inovações na Cidade do Rock, incluindo um telão de 2 mil metros quadrados no Palco Mundo e show da banda Foo Fighters.
articles.body:
Cidade do Rock recebe fãs de música a partir desta sexta-feira (4) — Foto: Josué Luz/ TV Globo

A Cidade do Rock, na Zona Oeste do Rio, está pronta para receber o público no primeiro dia do Rock in Rio. Na manhã desta sexta-feira (4), o espaço passava pelos últimos ajustes antes da abertura dos portões. A principal atração da noite no Palco Mundo será a banda Foo Fighters .

Segundo a vice-presidente da Rock World, empresa responsável pelo festival, Roberta Medina, a edição deste ano terá uma série de inovações tecnológicas que prometem transformar a experiência dos espectadores.

Entre os destaques está o novo Palco Mundo, equipado com um telão de LED de mais de 2 mil metros quadrados.

“É muito potente e, a partir de hoje, vamos ver cada artista transformar o Palco Mundo em um palco novo. Muita tecnologia. É o mundo das telas, mas com música ao vivo e emoção”, afirmou Roberta.

O evento conta com novidades como banheiros sem gênero e aplicativo interativo para ajudar quem vai ao evento.

O Foo Fighters encerra a programação do Palco Mundo na noite de abertura. Esta será a terceira apresentação da banda na Cidade do Rock. O grupo também participou das edições de 2001 e 2019 do festival.

A programação do palco principal inclui ainda o Rise Against, banda norte-americana de hardcore conhecida desde os anos 2000 pelas músicas de forte energia e letras com conteúdo político.

No Palco Sunset, os destaques ficam por conta do Capital Inicial e de Dado Villa-Lobos. O encontro promete celebrar o rock nacional, especialmente a tradição das bandas de Brasília, reunindo sucessos do Capital e clássicos da Legião Urbana.Festival estreia novo Palco Mundo, com telão de mais de 2 mil metros quadrados, e promete mudanças visuais a cada apresentação.

articles.body:
Público pode experiemntar carros na pista dusrante o Festival Interlagos. — Foto: Divulgação

O Festival Interlagos Edição Auto, que aconteceu entre os dias 27 e 30 de agosto, reuniu 215 mil visitantes e teve 36 lançamentos, pré-lançamentos e novidades apresentados ao público.

Edição Auto reuniu 32 marcas no Autódromo de Interlagos; somadas, as etapas de carro e motos tiveram 485 mil visitantes e 81 novidades.

Entre as empresas participantes estavam fabricantes tradicionais, marcas premium, esportivas e novas montadoras chinesas que estão ampliando a atuação no mercado brasileiro.

A edição Auto também permitiu que os visitantes dirigissem parte dos veículos apresentados. Foram 15,2 mil testes de direção realizados nas diferentes pistas preparadas para o evento.

Os testes ocorreram tanto no traçado de Interlagos quanto em áreas específicas destinadas a diferentes tipos de veículos e situações de condução.

O evento registrou 31,5 mil experiências de direção e pilotagem nas duas edições . O número considera os testes realizados pelos visitantes com carros e motos.

O número de 270 mil pessoas da edição de motos representa crescimento de aproximadamente 51% em relação a 2025 , quando 179 mil pessoas passaram pelo evento.

A proposta do evento é permitir que o público tenha contato direto com veículos que estão chegando ao mercado ou que já são vendidos no país. Além da exposição, parte dos modelos pôde ser conduzida pelos visitantes.

O calor do primeiro dia do Rock in Rio também influenciou o look dos fãs que foram ao festival. Quem chegou cedo à Cidade do Rock nesta sexta-feira (4) caprichou nas produções para enfrentar as altas temperaturas, curtir os shows e aproveitar o primeiro dia de festival.

As amigas Mariana e Gabriele apostaram em renda e transparência, mas com propostas diferentes.

Mariana escolheu um look com camadas e tule. A produção foi montada a partir de uma peça que recebeu e que serviu de inspiração para o restante da roupa.

“Eu trouxe uma das coisas que eu gosto de festival: renda, assimetria, camurça e bota”, explicou Mariana.

Gabriele também apostou na renda e na transparência para compor o visual. A produção, no entanto, acabou sendo mais quente do que Mariana imaginava.

“Eu não sabia o que esperar. Achei que poderia estar chovendo e esperava que estivesse mais fresco. Está mais quente do que eu imaginava. Não vejo a hora de tirar isso aqui”, brincou.

Mesmo com o calor, as amigas chegaram preparadas para passar o dia no festival e aproveitar a programação.

Mariana Gomes também decidiu apostar na criatividade para montar a produção. Ela veio ao festival por causa de um trabalho e precisava seguir uma paleta de cores específica. Como não tinha uma peça azul — sua cor preferida — e não poderia apostar no preto, decidiu buscar uma alternativa diferente. A solução foi transformar duas camisas em uma saia.

Mariana Gomes uniu duas camisas em uma saia — Foto: Jéssica Araújo/g1 Rio

“Comecei a procurar referências e lembrei que tinha salvado no Pinterest uma menina, inclusive aqui do Rio, uma blogueira, que tinha unido duas camisas e feito uma saia. Aí lembrei que tinha duas camisas e pensei: ‘Bom, então vai ser isso’”, contou.

A saia feita com as duas camisas virou a peça-chave do look.

Nicole escolheu um top preto e vermelho de veludo para ir ao Rock in Rio — Foto: Jéssica Araújo/g1 Rio

Nicole escolheu um top preto e vermelho de veludo, combinado com uma saia de tule preta. Para ela, as tradicionais camisetas pretas de bandas, apesar de combinarem com o estilo do festival, poderiam não ser a melhor opção para enfrentar o calor.

A escolha inicial foi o top, e a ideia era montar o restante do look a partir da peça. “A princípio, adorei”, contou, ao falar sobre a produção.

Jéssica usa calça de lurex metalizada — Foto: Jéssica Araújo/g1 Rio

Já Jéssica decidiu fugir do tradicional preto associado ao rock. Ela escolheu uma calça de lurex, tecido flexível com fios metalizados, combinada com uma blusa branca. A inspiração veio de uma peça que ela já havia usado em outros shows, mas a ideia era criar algo diferente para esta edição do festival.

“Achei que seria bem específico pelo tema do rock. Queria, esse ano, ser muito diferente e, na verdade, queria muito autenticidade no meu look. Queria fazer uma coisa muito diferente, mas que ainda lembrasse o rock. Foi exatamente a minha escolha. Eu quis sair do usual, do preto, e tentei colocar mais cor”, contou.

Apesar do calor, ela disse que a roupa não causa desconforto.

“Não está me incomodando absolutamente nada. Estou super tranquila”, afirmou.

articles.title: Birmingham music festival celebrates 20 year anniversary
articles.summary: The event, which has become a staple in the Midlands music diary, first appeared in 2006.
articles.body:
The Moseley Folk festival takes place this weekend with headliners Kingfishr, Super Furry Animals, and The Dead South all set to wow the crowds.

The event, which has become a staple in the Midlands music diary, first appeared in 2006.

It takes place in the secluded Moseley Park in Birmingham, and has seen headliners ranging from Donovan to Don Mclean, from Steeleye Span to Echo and the Bunnymen.

"It feels like your classic British festival in the countryside, but yet here it is right in the heart of the city, in this lush park, with a really cosy vibe", said Max Gittings, from folk group, The Destroyers.

He added: "We were just delighted to be invited."

Gittings' band, who hail from Birmingham, were well-received at the inaugural festival previously, due to their 'megafolk' style.

"We played this lovely chilled out afternoon set and it was among the first proper festivals we'd started to play at, the year before we did our first Glastonbury", he said.

The band have played at the festival many times since, and will be on stage again this year for the twentieth anniversary.

"It holds special memories, it was part of our beginnings.

"Just gathering at the lake backstage beforehand and then coming out to play for a really nice audience is great."

The Moseley Folk audience has grown from around 1,000 people two decades ago, to the 4,000 expected for 2026.

Festival organiser, John Fell, says that while the music is the key attraction, incorporating more food and drink has been an important step.

"Over the years we've changed by adding a few more stages, bringing in workshops, family areas...but the food scene in Birmingham has grown incredibly, so we've enveloped that as well and the crowds have got bigger and stronger every year."

Smaller boutique-style festivals have exploded across the UK in the last decade but they're not always easy to sustain.

Costs have inevitably risen, and with weekend tickets at £182 and day tickets £69 there are also some who could find it difficult to afford.

But Fell maintains it's very good value for what is being provided.

He says that the festival is passionate about supporting local artists and businesses.

"It's Brummies that run it. Everyone involved is local.

"That's a really proud thing for us to do because we have a national audience coming in seeing the best of Birmingham."

The twentieth edition of the Moseley Folk and Arts Festival incorporates aspects of comedy, poetry and wellness.

Twenty-nine acts played the first two-day festival in 2006, this year will see between 60 and 70 acts perform.

Fell thinks the event's legacy is secure.

He said: "There's so much going on in the world that live music is always going to be at the forefront of people wanting to get out there, experience [it] and have a good time.

"So thankfully we're involved in that process and I think we've got a good future to come."

articles.title: Barnsley travelling telephone box tells town's stories
articles.summary: A red telephone box which plays audio monologues from people in Barnsley is setting off on a tour.
articles.body:
A red telephone box which plays audio monologues of stories from people in Barnsley through a handset is setting off on a tour of the town.

The "Calling Barnsley" project was created by Lung Theatre group who recorded the monologues and built a life-sized phone box, which has been housed in the Barnsley Civic Arts Centre since January.

Now, the group is hoping to "share the stories" as the box embarks on a six-month tour of the town's libraries.

Matt Woodhead, theatre co-director, said, "There's a poeticism in the way that people in Barnsley speak. You can't knock about town without someone pulling your ear and telling you the most incredible story."

Co-director Helen Monks, said their box was wider than a typical public one in order to allow wheelchair access.

"Otherwise it looks the same. You still pick up the receiver and dial a different number depending on what story you want to hear," she explained.

The theatre group worked with students at Barnsley College to collect and record the two-minute stories through workshops over a two-year period.

The students also helped produce and direct vocal actors to transform them into monologues.

Woodhead said they managed to collect a "whole chocolate box" of stories.

He said: "We've got a gorgeous story about the Christmas lights of Thurnscoe, about how a community came together - and then, in contrast, the story of someone getting a kebab thrown at them when they're in town on a night out."

The kebab story was Dr Ryan Bramley's own personal experience as a student.

Now a lecturer in education at the University of Sheffield, Bramley, born in Barnsley was struck by a kebab on a night out because he was "wearing a smartish blazer".

The group managed to collect more than 60 stories in total, which were picked up by publishers Faber and Faber and turned into a book.

Monks said it was "the right time" for the phone box, which can be dismantled into five parts, to move.

"One of the things that we found is that people really see themselves as cultural people in Barnsley so it's really important that the phone doesn't just sit in the town centre but it goes to all of people's local areas".

From 4 September, the phone box's new home for a month will be The Lightbox at Barnsley Central Library before moving on to libraries in Royston, Cudworth, Atherley, Goldthorpe and Penistone over the next six months.

It will also be stopping at Persistence Works Sheffield as part of University of Sheffield's Festival of the Mind.

Woodhead said the long-term home for the phone box was unknown but that this was "just the start of a conversation".

"This phone box is a beautiful celebration of Barnsley but you also don't need the phone box to go and tell your story. There's so many people that have got a story to tell so you have to get right in and start telling it," he added.

articles.title: La tremenda pelea entre Marcos de Quinto y Afra Blanca en ‘Espejo Público’: “Cuando yo intervengo pone caritas de payasa”
articles.standfirst: El empresario y la sindicalista discuten en directo en el espacio de Antena 3
articles.summary: El empresario y la sindicalista discuten en directo en el espacio de Antena 3
articles.body: Este viernes, 4 de septiembre, el plató de ‘Espejo Público’ ha vivido una de las mayores broncas del año en el programa matinal de Antena 3 que presenta Susanna Griso. Mientras se debatía acerca de la crisis migratoria en Ceuta, Marcos de Quinto y Afra Blanco han protagonizado una pelea que ha obligado a intervenir a la conductora del espacio ante la sorpresa de todos los presentes. Todo ha ocurrido cuando Griso ha pedido a Blanco que hablara sobre los informes del CENIF, pero las primeras palabras de la sindicalista han ido dirigidas a su compañero: “Lamento tener que romper la dinámica del debate. He pasado todo el verano criticando la gestión de esta crisis, pero… Marcos, qué elegante te presentas aquí hoy, ¿eh?”. Ante el silencio del empresario, ha proseguido: “Pero después, Marcos de Quinto tiene otra versión. Supongo que la valentía y la gallardía se la ha dejado en el fondo de un botellín, en ese yate”. Tras ello, ha justificado su ataque por los supuestos insultos de su compañero en redes sociales: “Digo esto porque somos cinco mujeres en esta mesa, que discrepamos, que debatimos y que supongo que continuamente sufrimos ataques, denigración, cosificación e insultos en redes sociales”. Cuando Afra Blanco ha pedido a Marcos de Quinto que aplicara esa misma valentía en persona, el empresario no se ha quedado callado. “Continuamente, cuando yo intervengo en este programa, ella se pone a hacer caritas de payasa. Es una cosa que me disgusta”, ha aseverado. “Y yo tengo una pregunta para Afra: ¿Habéis devuelto los de la UGT los 40 millones que robasteis al fondo de parados en Andalucía y que está firme por sentencia del Tribunal Supremo?”, ha replicado el empresario, que ha zanjado: “Discúlpate por poner caritas. Afra, que eres una broncas, estás a broncas con todo el mundo”.

articles.title: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle’s school warning letters reignite privacy battle they ‘cannot control’: experts
articles.summary: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle's children Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet are reportedly starting private school in the Cotswolds, prompting warning letters to parents about privacy rules.
articles.body: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle’s return to the United Kingdom could become their biggest privacy test yet as their children Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet begin school life in the English countryside. Last week, Markle, 45, and Harry, 41, along with their son Archie, 7, and daughter Princess Lilibet, 5, left their home in Montecito, California, for an extended stay in Britain. According to reports, the Duke and Duchess of Sussex plan to settle in the Cotswolds, an affluent countryside region in south-central England, located about two hours outside London. Archie and Lilibet are reportedly set to begin classes at a private school in the U.K., though the school has not been publicly named. PRINCE HARRY AND MEGHAN MARKLE ARRIVE IN UK WITH KIDS, MARKING DRAMATIC RETURN 6 YEARS AFTER ROYAL EXIT In a report published Monday, royal commentator Kinsey Schofield told Page Six that parents in the Cotswolds area received warning letters from school officials after Harry and Markle "approached multiple schools" for Archie and Lilibet ahead of their move. The letters reportedly reminded families of privacy rules surrounding students and high-profile families. PRINCE HARRY AND MEGHAN MARKLE WON’T ‘HIJACK’ PRINCE GEORGE’S HISTORIC ETON DEBUT, ROYAL EXPERT SAYS "The message sent to families essentially said that, from time to time, some families joining the school may attract a greater level of public or media interest," Schofield told the outlet. The message also reportedly noted that the school wanted to preserve a "safe, happy, and private environment" for all students. MEGHAN MARKLE’S UK RETURN POSES PALACE CONTROL ‘NIGHTMARE,’ EXPERT WARNS "It then reminded parents and carers not to photograph or film other children without permission, or share photographs, information or details about pupils or their families on social media," Schofield said. Page Six did not identify the school that sent the letters, citing privacy concerns, but reported that it is not the school Archie and Lilibet are attending. PRINCE WILLIAM 'NO LONGER RECOGNIZES' PRINCE HARRY AS SECURITY BATTLE LEAVES DUKE 'CLOSE TO TEARS': EXPERT Harry and Markle have long tried to shield their children from uncontrolled public exposure. The couple has previously skipped the traditional royal baby photo call, limited public images of their children and raised security concerns around U.K. visits. However, royal experts told Fox News Digital that school life presents a different challenge because it places Archie and Lilibet’s privacy partly in the hands of other parents, classmates and the broader community. PRINCE WILLIAM LIKELY 'LIVID' OVER MEGHAN MARKLE'S 'TASTELESS' PHOTOS AT PRINCESS DIANA'S HOME: EXPERT Schofield, who also spoke to Fox News Digital about the couple’s return to Britain, said the school warnings underscore how difficult it may be for Harry and Markle to manage their children’s privacy in everyday settings. "School introduces an enormous number of variables Harry and Meghan cannot control," the host of YouTube’s "Kinsey Schofield Unfiltered" said. "Other parents have phones. Children have friends. There are school events, sporting fixtures, birthday parties, drop-offs, and pick-ups," Schofield added. "You cannot manage a school community like a communications operation." Schofield noted that the letter she had seen was "deliberately vague" but explained that the reminders were likely not unusual on their own. However, she argued that the attention surrounding Harry and Markle will change the dynamic for other families. "None of those requests are unreasonable," Schofield continued. "Archie and Lili deserve exactly the same opportunity as every other child to go to school without feeling watched. But inevitably, when one family attracts this level of global attention, the entire school community becomes more conscious of what it photographs, posts, and discusses." "Other families are effectively being asked to adjust their behavior because Harry and Meghan have arrived," she added. PRINCE WILLIAM, KATE MIDDLETON FACE 'SUSSEX CIRCUS' AS PRINCE GEORGE PREPARES FOR ETON: EXPERT While speaking with Fox News Digital, royal expert Hilary Fordwich pointed out that Markle posted photos of Archie and Lilibet on her own social media, sharing her view that it was "beyond hypocritical to on the one hand want ‘privacy’ yet on the other hand, monetize their family." While Markle has shared photos of her children on Instagram, they are often pictured from behind, with their faces hidden or in carefully chosen images. The former "Suits" star’s representative previously defended Markle’s approach in a statement to Newsweek. "The Duchess has always been clear that there is a distinction between sharing moments from her life and exposing her children to public scrutiny," her spokesperson said in June. "By obscuring their faces, she is demonstrating the very principle she advocates for: giving children privacy, agency, and protection in an increasingly digital world." articles.title: Gasly loses Monaco podium after McLaren and Red Bull win appeals
articles.summary: McLaren and Red Bull win their appeals against the result of the Monaco Grand Prix after a controversy over multiple incorrect pit-lane speeding penalties.
articles.body:
McLaren and Red Bull have won their appeals against the result of the Monaco Grand Prix after a controversy over multiple incorrect pit-lane speeding penalties.

The victory means Alpine's Pierre Gasly loses the podium he was awarded after an appeal by the French team that overturned two five-second penalties.

That means Gasly, who finished third on the road, is dropped back to the seventh place he received in the official results.

Red Bull's Isack Hadjar is returned to third place and McLaren's Oscar Piastri fourth, with Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad moving up to fifth and sixth.

However, the verdict does not fully address the multiple effects of a series of pit-lane speeding penalties.

These affected the results of many drivers in the race, including Mercedes' George Russell.

The Briton was dropped out of the points for a penalty he received for not correctly serving a pit-lane speeding penalty.

The court of appeal decision rests on its conclusion that the parameters for measuring a limit could not be changed in the midst of a grand prix weekend once competitors had been informed of them.

The discrepancy between the official F1 measurement and the possible shorter distance did not mean that the official measurement was incorrect, the court said.

The finding was that, while it was concluded after the race that a shorter line was possible, "what sporting fairness absolutely precludes is the retrospective replacement, after competitors have calibrated and competed against it, of the common event-wide calibration parameter itself by a different geometric or measurement approach for the purpose of re-adjudicating an individual competitor's result".

The controversy arose from the fact that there was a 77-centimetre discrepancy between the officially measured distance of the pit lane and the real shortest route a driver could legally take.

It was established at Alpine's appeal that Gasly had not exceeded the pit-lane speeding limit by this new measurement, which was why the penalty was overturned.

However, McLaren appealed on the grounds of sporting fairness and their own competitive interests, as Piastri had lost two points as a consequence of the situation.

The Australian was one of the drivers who did serve a five-second pit-lane speeding penalty.

Alpine said in a statement: "While we disagree with the decision, and still fully maintain that car 10 (Gasly) did not exceed the pit-lane speed limit at any point during the race, the team acknowledges the decision of the judging panel from the recent hearing in Paris.

"While the result is not what we had hoped for, as we feel that we have been unjustly punished, the team is firmly focused on continuing to improve its performance on track and remains in a close and very competitive championship fight."
authors: Andrew Benson - F1 Correspondent at Monza

articles.title: Tiffany Haddish once lived out of her car and survived on $500 a month; after a stranger told her to buy property with every movie paycheck, she now owns about 17
articles.summary: Comedian and actor Tiffany Haddish says an unexpected conversation with an accountant changed the way she thought about money and property. Today, she.
articles.body: Comedian and actor Tiffany Haddish says an unexpected conversation with an accountant changed the way she thought about money and property. Today, she owns about 17 properties, but her approach to real estate began after years of financial uncertainty.Haddish recently spoke about her property investments during a live recording of the podcast 'Family Trips With the Meyers Brothers', Realtor reported. Seth Meyers and his brother, Josh Meyers, asked her about the kind of holidays she enjoys. Haddish said she likes travelling in groups and still uses Groupon to find discounted trips.One such trip took her to China and Japan. It was during that group holiday that she met an accountant who gave her advice that stayed with her. The accountant suggested she read “The Weekend Millionaire’s Secrets to Investing in Real Estate: How to Become Wealthy in Your Spare Time”, by Mike Summey and Roger Dawson.The accountant told her “If you’re doing movies and you think you’re going to make it, when you start making money, buy a piece of property every year for 15 years. No matter what happens with your career, you’ll be successful. They can never cancel you or stop you,” Haddish recalled.Haddish’s Real Estate JourneyHaddish said she followed that advice by buying property when she earned money from her acting career. She now has “like 17” properties in her portfolio and said she buys one whenever she stars in a movie.She also explained why she believes owning land can provide financial security. “If you have land, you’ll be a multimillionaire, even with 10 properties,” she said.Her current property holdings are a major change from the period when she struggled to find stable housing. Haddish has previously spoken about experiencing homelessness during the early part of her comedy career. She has also discussed spending time in foster care as a child.One of the people who helped her during that difficult period was fellow comedian Kevin Hart. Haddish spoke about this in a 2024 appearance on “This Life of Mine With James Cordon”.Kevin Hart Helped Her Find HomeAt the time, Haddish was performing sketch comedy shows with Hart at the Laugh Factory in Los Angeles. Hart noticed that her car was filled with her belongings and began to suspect that she was experiencing homelessness.Haddish said she tried to avoid discussing her situation with him. She would arrive late because she did not want other people to see her car and realise that she was living in it.“I would show up late. I didn’t want nobody to see my car. I would park a little farther away, or I would pull up and let the valet take the car, but I would pull up late so nobody would see,” she said.Hart eventually confronted the situation. He gave Haddish $300 that night, which she used to pay for a hotel room. He then connected her with a real estate agent who could help her find a place to live.The apartment she eventually found was far from ideal. Haddish said it needed extensive work and described its condition as poor.“It needed so much work,” she said. “It was disgusting, and I looked around and I was like, ‘Wow.’ I saw roaches. It was bad.” Despite its condition, the apartment gave her an affordable place to stay. The rent was $500 a month, so Haddish decided to take it.“I still have that place,” she confirmed in 2024. “I still have it. I had to fix it up myself and I still got it.”Paying Off Her First HouseHaddish later used a similar focus on property when she started earning more from acting. In a 2022 interview with Cosmopolitan, she described how she bought her first house after appearing on “The Carmichael Show” in 2015.She said people around her advised her to wait before buying a house. Haddish chose to move ahead because she wanted to make sure she could support herself and maintain the property.“Before we even got into Season 2 of ‘The Carmichael Show,’ I bought a house,” she said. “Everybody told me I should wait, but I didn’t care. I just knew I was going to have to always make enough money to take care of me and the house, and that’s what I did.”Her next acting projects helped her pay down the cost of the property. Haddish said she kept her personal spending low and was able to live comfortably on $500 a month during that period.“Between that show’s next season, the ‘Keanu’ movie, and making sure I can live comfortably off of $500 a month, I was able to pay off half the house,” she said.The money she earned from “Girls Trip” then helped her finish paying off the house. Haddish said she had been advised to use the money in other ways, but she chose to put it towards the property.“The ‘Girls Trip’ check was the final check. People told me to spend it other ways, but I used it to pay off the house because I was always afraid of being homeless again,” she saidAlthough Haddish now has a surplus of money because of her success, she has said she remains conscious of her finances. She also told Cosmopolitan that she would eventually like to retire and buy a ranch in Wyoming.Give your child the gift of confidence! Claim your exclusive TOI Masterclass spot today!

articles.title: New movies to watch this weekend: See 'Onslaught' in theaters, rent 'I Want Your Sex,' stream 'The Runner' on Prime Video
articles.summary: Adria Arjona's action horror flick "Onslaught" is the week's big movie release, while Mark Wahlberg and Gal Gadot helm new films of their own.
articles.body:
Welcome to Trust Me, I Watch Everything , a weekly guide to all the new movies out each Friday.

This week's buzziest release is likely A24's Onslaught, an exploitation action horror flick that's worth a watch despite some problems. The survival thriller sequel Fall 2: Deadpoint also makes its way to theaters.

If you'd rather stay home, you can now rent or buy I Want Your Sex, Gregg Araki's sex comedy farce with Olivia Wilde and Cooper Hoffman, and The Wrong Girls, a stoner comedy with Kristen Stewart and Alia Shawkat.

Want to stick to a streaming service you're likely already paying for? The straight-to-streaming Gal Gadot vehicle The Runner debuts on Prime Video, and the latest Star Wars movie, The Mandalorian and Grogu, is now airing on Disney+.

Why I liked it, with reservations: Onslaught sees filmmaker Adam Wingard returning to his roots, giving up a Godzilla vs. Kong- sized studio blockbuster budget to instead make a relatively cheap and dirty '80s-style exploitation movie throwback, complete with John Carpenter movie font for its opening titles. Wingard has teased that the movie takes place in the same town as his cult favorite The Guest, and both feature Dan Stevens in different key roles. But make no mistake: Onslaught is 100% Adria Arjona's movie.

Onslaught is a delightfully unsubtle exploitation action horror movie about a U.S. government that's occupied by Nazis, killing its own citizens and manipulating its veterans. When a rogue squad of genetically engineered super-soldiers breaks loose in the desert, a badass Army sniper (Arjona) must unleash hell to protect her young daughter. The three super-soldiers are given the slasher-movie villain treatment; they're unstoppable killing machines who act like "heat-seeking missiles" toward whatever their objective may be. Imagine The Terminator, but there are three of them!

It's a lot of fun if you're into this sort of thing, and the constantly pulsing imitation John Carpenter synth score makes it feel bigger than it actually is. The biggest issue with the movie is entirely self-imposed: It prominently features a countdown clock ticking down to a sequence that ultimately doesn't live up to expectations when time runs out.

It feels like it's missing a barnburner finale, even if the gunplay and action are otherwise satisfying enough. Had the movie not insisted upon repeatedly saying "buckle up, audience, you're not going to believe this s**t," maybe the ending would've been thrilling enough. But after all that build-up, it can't help but feel like a bit of a letdown.

There's so much going on in the periphery of this movie. Rebecca Hall's character is a hoot but underutilized, Drew Starkey's goofy subplot really made me laugh but felt misplaced and Dan Stevens's evil Nazi doctor looks like an anime villain. It's a shame that it all comes off a little too straightforward, despite these occasional wacky elements.

Onslaught is perfectly entertaining for what it is, though it feels like the movie fails on its own terms by not living up to the expectations it set up for itself. It's as if Babe Ruth stepped up to the plate, called his shot and then hit a double. You'd appreciate that he got on base, but you'd probably be a little underwhelmed.

What other critics are saying : The reviews skew positive, but there are plenty of naysayers. T he Daily Beast's Nick Schager calls it "a hodgepodge of everything genre fans adore." Jake Coyle at the AP, however, writes that, "Even though Onslaught begins with a clock that's already ticking below 12 hours, the movie takes its time leading to a bloody finale that isn't quite worth the drumbeat."

How to watch : Onslaught is now playing in theaters nationwide .

Why I liked it: Must a movie be good to be entertaining and effective? Fall 2: Deadpoint is so clunky in every way, except the only one that really matters, that it may have you asking this question throughout.

2022's Fall worked because it made your palms sweaty in the way all good survival horror does: the situation, in which two girls are stuck 2,000 feet in the air on a radio tower, is inherently terrifying, and the movie works despite its cheapness and occasional bad CGI and phony green screen. It largely looks convincing and made me yell out loud multiple times. If you're even mildly afraid of heights, it'll mess you up.

That brings us to Fall 2: Deadpoint . On a perilous climb across Thailand's Mount Kwan, two climbers become trapped thousands of feet above the ground, where vertigo-inducing heights, sheer exposure and impossible odds turn every moment into a fight for survival.

Once again, it's an outrageously dangerous setup. Twin filmmaking duo Michael and Peter Spierig do a good job with a tight budget of putting the audience there and making it feel believable; it gives you that pit in your stomach during its best moments. The problem is that anytime it's not putting you on the edge of your seat, it's making you laugh at it, not with it, at the soap-opera-level melodrama unfolding onscreen.

The reverence this movie shows for the lead of the first movie, whom I didn't remember at all, is laugh-out-loud funny. The characters here all treat her like an iconic celebrity who deeply impacted the lives of millions due to her exploits in the first movie. There's atrocious dialogue throughout, including an attempt at a dramatic emotional reveal that made the entire audience cackle. The unfathomable choices these characters make throughout are a whole other can of worms.

But does any of that matter when the titular falling, and what have you, delivers as much intensity as ever?! It's tense and suspenseful, and I believed in the moment that the characters were in peril. (The number of shots of screws loosening is rivaled only by the Final Destination franchise.) It goes a bit too far in the third act with some extra manufactured drama, but I'd be lying if I didn't walk out excited for the already-planned third movie that's teased at the end here.

Fall 2: Deadpoint really pushes the limits of how silly a B-movie can get as long as it's delivering the goods, but it's brisk and has enough thrills to recommend to fans of the original and/or the genre.

What other critics are saying: Reviews aren't as kind as they were for the original. Simon Abrams at the AV Club writes, "This thankless sequel's highs simply aren't high enough." TheWrap's William Bibbiani was more on its wavelength, writing that "Once you embrace the Die Hard 2 ' of it all [...] it's easy to forgive this schlocky sequel for being, God forbid, a schlocky sequel."

How to watch: Fall 2: Deadpoint is now playing in theaters nationwide.

By Any Means: Mark Wahlberg gets top billing, but his prosthetic nose and toothpick do most of the heavy lifting in By Any Means, a '60s-set movie that can best be described as " Green Book but with mob violence." A young Black FBI agent (Yahya Abdul-Mateen II) is sent to Mississippi to investigate a wave of brutal killings targeting civil rights leaders. Forced to work alongside notorious mafia hitman Greg Scarpa (Wahlberg), he finds himself pulled into a deadly hunt where justice and vengeance begin to blur. It's based on a true story, but Wahlberg's turn as Scarpa is more a caricature of a Brooklyn mobster than a thoughtful portrayal of an interesting character. It's no Mississippi Burning. Get tickets.

Why I liked it, despite some issues: Gregg Araki's I Want Your Sex doesn't want to be taken too seriously, though its director's compassionate plea to Gen Z, specifically, is earnest and direct: Stop being afraid of sex. Allow yourself the experience of doing it, and accept all the pluses and minuses that come along with it, because these are the formative experiences of your life.

When fresh-faced Elliot (Cooper Hoffman) lands an exciting job for renowned artist, icon and provocateur Erika Tracy (Olivia Wilde, having a ball), his fantasies come true as Erika taps him to become her sexual muse. But Elliot soon finds himself out of his depth as Erika takes him on a journey more profound than he ever could have imagined, into a world of sex, obsession, power, betrayal and murder.

It's a sex-positive comedy that's more interested in earning laughs from the various sub-dom relationship situations the characters find themselves in than in actually depicting intimacy and sexiness, though Wilde is undeniably sexy and in her element here. By the third or fourth joke about her shoving stuff up Hoffman's ass, though, I started to see the limits of its edginess. Any fan of indie filmmaking knows that Gregg Araki ( The Doom Generation, Mysterious Skin ) can go way, way harder than this.

The movie's Sunset Boulevard -inspired frame narrative and flashback structure are its weakest assets. The Norma Desmond comparison is fun, but the movie doesn't really have any real reason to do the in medias res thing, and every time we cut to the interrogation room where two cops are getting the story out of Elliot, it kills the momentum and reminds you this is leading somewhere specific that's not necessarily in this particular movie's wheelhouse. The art world satire also feels a bit stale.

Where the movie shines, though, is in its depiction of a generation that came of age during the COVID-19 pandemic and how that experience stunted and deeply affected their sense of intimacy and their capacity for vulnerability. Oddly enough, I Want Your Sex actually has the same ultimate message as Toy Story 5: G et out from behind your smartphone and make a real, human connection. There's simply no replacement for it!

What other critics are saying: Reviews are quite positive, even if most use the same qualifying language I did. The Los Angeles Times' Amy Nicholson writes, "From the opening shot of a body in a Los Angeles pool, Araki and co-screenwriter Karley Sciortino tickle us with their 21st-century send-up of Sunset Boulevard . But Araki can go where Code-era movies couldn't: into the bedroom." Monica Castillo at the AV Club writes, "Araki's silly, sexy, tongue-in-cheek skewering of cross-generational sexual attitudes is just as funny as it is thought-provoking."

How to watch: I Want Your Sex is now available to rent or buy on Apple TV , Prime Video and other VOD platforms.

Why you should skip it: While this has nothing to do with Drive-Away Dolls or Honey, Don't, the lesbian caper comedies directed by Ethan Coen and his wife, it does feel like it's spiritually the capstone of that trilogy. Sadly, this is not a compliment. It also desperately wants what the unexpectedly hilarious Pizza Movie has.

In this stoner comedy directed by Kristen Stewart's wife, Dylan Meyer, two best friends living paycheck to paycheck and bong rip to bong rip get caught in a case of mistaken identity that throws their lives into chaos. Shawkat, in particular, is very funny here, earning laughs by simply saying her lines in silly, stoned ways.

It's almost respectable how low this movie's ambitions are, but it needs far more laughs than we get here to pull that off. The plotting is just so generic, derivative and unengaging, and the writing uninspired in a way that feels intentionally stupid but not funny. A major disappointment! Check out Smiley Face instead.

What other critics are saying: Reviewers are split right down the middle. Amy Nicholson at the Los Angeles Times calls it "the right comedy if you want to unplug your brain and laugh." The AV Club's Monica Castillo , though, writes: "All that action comes at the expense of the jokes, or at least funny ones, and by the movie's end, it's mostly a relief that the trip is finally over."

How to watch: The Wrong Girls is now available to rent or buy on Apple TV , Prime Video and other VOD platforms.

The Brink of War: More like the brink of snore! Jeff Daniels plays Ronald Reagan and Jared Harris plays Mikhail Gorbachev in this boring movie about a meeting. In the film, which lionizes Reagan, the U.S. president races against time to salvage a deal with the Soviet leader that could dismantle nuclear arsenals — or ignite disaster. With pressure mounting on all sides, every word spoken brings the world closer to peace … or destruction. It unfolds like a stage play, a two-hander that's simply an exchange of dialogue, but it's never compelling. The way the characters' wives are included is a bizarre bit of comic relief that doesn't fit the tone of the rest. Rent or buy .

📺 Movies newly available on streaming services you may already have

Why you should skip it: Gal Gadot is front and center in this Phone Booth knockoff for the Bluetooth age, and the movie is all the worse for it. She simply isn't a strong enough actor to carry a movie in which she's essentially in every single frame.

Gadot plays a high-powered attorney forced to race through London as she follows the cryptic commands of a mysterious caller (voiced by Damian Lewis) and fights against time to save her abducted son. Her son has been kidnapped as part of a scheme involving a crime boss who is on trial. She's the lawyer in the case, and the guy on the phone wants her to kill a high-profile witness. The convoluted plot makes less sense the more you consider it.

The action is all fairly light and limp, and director Kevin Macdonald — the documentarian-turned-feature-filmmaker who won an Oscar for his doc One Day in September — has a tough time livening up the proceedings. It's hardly his fault, though, as Gadot is simply never convincing, and her line readings of the not particularly good dialogue from the rote script are often laughable. It's a decidedly B-movie that fails the modest assignment of delivering engaging, cheap thrills.

Oddly enough, there's another movie with the title Runner, starring Alan Ritchson and Owen Wilson, out in theaters next week. That movie is, quite unexpectedly, a blast; Gadot's couldn't be further from one. If you want to watch a good movie with this basic premise, try Phone Booth, Cellular, Carry-On or even Nick of Time.

What other critics are saying: They're unforgiving! The Guardian's Ben Lee writes, "Intelligence might not be what one would expect here, which is somewhat acceptable in B-movie territory such as this, but the lack of excitement is hard to forgive." Jordan Mintzer at the Hollywood Reporter is the outlier, writing that "Movies such as these are all about suspension of disbelief, and The Runner keeps a fast enough pace that we don't wind up asking too many questions."

How to watch: The Runner is now streaming on Prime Video .

Another option: The Mandalorian and Grogu

Why I didn't like it: The Mandalorian and Grogu is easily the worst Star Wars movie, but even calling it a movie feels like giving it more credit than it deserves. It's a feature-length episode of streaming-era television, and boy, does it look and feel like it. It's uncinematic in pretty much every way, from the drab visuals to its repetitive structure that lacks the storytelling heft needed to make the jump from TV to film. Say what you will about The Rise of Skywalker or the prequel trilogy; at least they're movies!

An extension of the Disney+ streaming series The Mandalorian , The Mandalorian and Grogu takes place between the original and sequel trilogies. Onscreen text, although not in the iconic crawl you may be expecting, indicates that the evil Empire has fallen, and Imperial warlords remain scattered throughout the galaxy. As the fledgling New Republic works to protect everything the Rebellion fought for, they have enlisted the help of legendary Mandalorian bounty hunter Din Djarin and his young apprentice, Grogu.

The "Mandalorian" distinction means the lead character is masked, and Pedro Pascal's flat vocal performance doesn't do much to compensate for it. And although his co-lead is a puppet, a great throwback to the way these kinds of movies used to be made, there are even more entirely-CGI creations throughout. This may be in the grand Lucasian tradition, but still not as effective as, say, a tall guy in a hairy dog suit. This movie's Chewbacca is some purple CGI guy!

There's no real work done to upgrade the material for the big screen, so it just plays like binge-watching a few episodes of the show, with no real driving narrative force to keep you engaged. One of the plots — it's not the plot because, remember, this movie is really just TV — revolves around Jabba the Hutt's muscular outcast son, who actually utters something along the lines of, "Do you know how hard it is to be Jabba the Hutt's son?" and talks about how he's his own man in spite of his upbringing. The character is played by The Bear star and current hunk of the moment, Jeremy Allen White. Who is this for? Instead of leaning into the Andor direction that won praise, Lucasfilm has circled back to the safe space of "cute puppet antics" and nostalgic nudges.

Composer and three-time Oscar winner Ludwig Göransson is the only one to come out of this unscathed, as his terrific score does all the heavy lifting, giving the movie gravitas and energy at key moments when it otherwise has none.

When award-winning creatives like Steven Soderbergh and Damon Lindelof are openly discussing Star Wars projects falling apart, and the actual output at Disney is The Mandalorian and Grogu, a nothing movie with low stakes more concerned with selling plush dolls than appealing to newcomers or casual fans, something has gone wrong. What was once a can't-miss theatrical event every time, as recently as 11 years ago — The Force Awakens is the highest-grossing movie ever in this country to this day — is now debuting with a collective shrug. This isn't the way.

What other critics are saying: They're split right down the middle, although even the positive ones aren't super effusive or enthusiastic. Slate's Sam Adams writes: "If The Mandalorian and Grogu isn't the worst Star Wars movie — and it might be — it's certainly the least: the least essential, the least engaging, the least necessary." Robert Abele at the Los Angeles Times was kinder, writing: "One of the movie's strong points, absent its story deficiencies, is that, across its many wordless scenes, it's at heart a solidly rousing, delightfully icky creature feature, in the vein of a supercharged Ray Harryhausen-meets-Guillermo del Toro joint."

How to watch: The Mandalorian and Grogu is now streaming on Disney+ .

Mayday : Your tolerance for Ryan Reynolds smarmy one-liners will determine whether or not you enjoy this period action-comedy starring Reynolds and Kenneth Branagh. When a U.S. Navy pilot on a top-secret mission during the Cold War gets trapped behind enemy lines, his only chance at survival is to form an alliance with an eccentric ex-KGB agent. Branagh doing a silly Russian accent is fun — an esteemed actor and director such as himself slumming it and being silly in something like this wrings some laughs out of the otherwise tired material — but too much of the comedy relies on Reynolds's shtick, which grew tired a few presidential administrations ago. It has better-than-your-average-streaming-movie action sequences, though, thanks to directing team John Francis Daley and Jonathan Goldstein, the pair responsible for the terrific Game Night and the beloved Dungeons & Dragons movie from a couple of years ago. It's OK! Now streaming on Apple TV .

Scary Movie : Scary Movie, aka Scary Movie 6, is the first new entry in the parody franchise in 13 years, and the first Wayans brothers entry in 25. Unfortunately, their return to the smash-hit series is a reminder that maybe some things are better left in the past and that references in and of themselves are not jokes. Barring a Final Destination sight gag up top that made me laugh, and a third-act Scream -style reveal that works (but would've worked better had the movie not already made that joke earlier), Scary Movie is an embarrassing cash-grab nostalgia play that feels like every single element onscreen is the first draft. Read my full review here. Now streaming on Paramount+ .

Signal One: This no-budget sci-fi indie gem you've never heard of is totally worth watching, and boasts a great cast. A computer scientist is invited by a tech billionaire to join his private facility on a Caribbean island to investigate extraterrestrial matter on Earth. When they make contact beyond our world, chaos erupts, leaving us to wonder: Do they come in peace? It stars Dennis Quaid, Isabelle Fuhrman, Josh Hutcherson and David Thewlis, and is so much better than similar low-budget fare. Signal One may be in familiar and well-worn territory, but it actually engages with its heady concepts in exciting new ways. Now streaming on Hulu .

Fuze: The plot of Fuze is simple yet also more complex than it appears at first glance. It's a tense, ticking-clock thriller about an unexploded WWII bomb that is discovered on a busy construction site in the middle of London. Chaos ensues as the military and police begin a mass evacuation, and the true nature of the situation gets revealed. Now it's a heist movie! It's an incredibly efficient and propulsive flick that keeps you invested as more complications are revealed. Aaron Taylor-Johnson stars as the guy defusing the bomb, and Sam Worthington and Theo James show up as the criminals committing a robbery, using the bomb situation as cover. It's directed by David Mackenzie, who was behind the Taylor Sheridan-penned Hell or High Water. The cross-cutting and editing here really keep things moving along; it's a brass-tacks genre exercise and nothing more, but it succeeds within those parameters. Now streaming on HBO Max.

That's all for this week! We'll see you next Friday — just in time for Practical Magic 2.

articles.title: Richard O'Sullivan, ‘Man About The House’ actor passes away at the age of 82
articles.summary: Richard O'Sullivan, best known for playing Robin Tripp in the 1970s sitcoms ‘Man About the House’ and Robin's Nest’, has passed away at the age of 82..
articles.body: Richard O'Sullivan, best known for playing Robin Tripp in the 1970s sitcoms ‘Man About the House’ and Robin's Nest’, has passed away at the age of 82. Over his career, he also took on notable roles in ‘Doctor at Large’, ‘Dick Turpin’, and the 1980s sitcom ‘Me and My Girl’, sharing the screen with Tim Brooke-Taylor, Joanne Ridley, and Joan Sanderson.Richard O'Sullivan passes away at Brinsworth HouseAccording to BBC, O'Sullivan passed away with close family by his side at Brinsworth House, the Royal Variety Charity's care home in west London, where he had made his home for the past 23 years.Royal Variety Charity pays tribute to Richard O'SullivanGiles Cooper of the Royal Variety Charity paid tribute in a statement, saying: "Richard O'Sullivan was a master of effortless charm and impeccable comic timing, bringing pure warmth, wit, and unforgettable joy to millions of living rooms as a true giant of British television." Cooper further noted that O'Sullivan would be "sorely missed by us all at the Royal Variety Charity".Richard O'Sullivan's son remembers him fondlyThe actor's son, James O'Sullivan, shared his own tribute, saying: "My dad was as funny and charming in real life as he appeared on our TV screens over the years. Although much of his career happened before I was born, I was fortunate enough to be able to enjoy and witness his incredible talents on the countless re-runs of his shows that made him the respected and loved actor that he was." He also expressed gratitude to the staff at Brinsworth House for their "love, kindness and care".Richard O'Sullivan's most memorable TV rolesSet around a man cohabiting with two single women in a London flat, a fairly daring concept for its time, ‘Man About the House’ ran for six series on ITV, with O'Sullivan starring alongside Paula Wilcox, Sally Thomsett, Yootha Joyce, and Brian Murphy. In ‘Me and My Girl’, he played a different role altogether, that of a widower bringing up his teenage daughter.Richard O'Sullivan's early life and career beginningsO'Sullivan, born in London in 1944, began acting as a child in the 1950s and 60s, taking on uncredited parts in dramas as early as 1953. He later featured in ‘Raiders of the River’, the Children's Film Foundation's debut serial, and in 1956 appeared in Sir Peter Hall's staging of ‘Love's Labour's Lost’ at the Royal Shakespeare Theatre in Stratford. His credits also include the 1961 drama Spare the Rod, a social commentary starring Max Bygraves and Donald Pleasance about a teacher working in a deprived, challenging area, in which O'Sullivan portrayed a rebellious, difficult student in his final year. After building steady momentum with dramatic parts, including playing Pharaoh Ptolemy XIII in 1963's ‘Cleopatra’ alongside Elizabeth Taylor and Richard Burton, he shifted towards comedy, appearing in shows like ‘The Ronnie Barker Playhouse’ in 1968 and ‘The Galton’ and ‘Simpson Comedy’ the year after.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: Sydney Sweeney y Scooter Braun derrochan amor y complicidad en el Festival de Venecia
articles.standfirst: La actriz ha acudido como embajadora de la marca Armani Beauty
articles.summary: La actriz ha acudido como embajadora de la marca Armani Beauty
articles.body: Sydney Sweeney es, sin duda, la actriz del momento. Sin embargo, esta vez no es tendencia por algún proyecto profesional, sino por su aparición pública con su novio, el empresario Scooter Braun. Ambos han acaparado todas las miradas en el Festival de Cine de Venecia 2026, donde han sido pillados compartiendo besos, miradas cómplices y un romántico paseo en góndola por los icónicos canales venecianos. La protagonista de ‘Euphoria’, que asiste al certamen cinematográfico como embajadora de la marca Armani Beauty, aprovechó el viaje para celebrar su primer año de relación con Braun. A ambos se les vio muy sonrientes y relajados en todo momento, ajenos por completo a las cámaras de los fotógrafos mientras recorrían la ciudad tanto en transporte acuático como a pie. La historia de amor entre Sydney Sweeney y Scooter Braun comenzó con un auténtico flechazo en Venecia en junio de 2025, la misma ciudad en la que hoy celebran su primer aniversario. Ambos coincidieron como invitados en la lujosa e íntima boda de Jeff Bezos y Lauren Sánchez. La química entre la intérprete estadounidense y el mánager musical fue inmediata; de hecho, fuentes cercanas revelaron a portales como Page Six que Braun quedó fascinado tras conocerla. Después de ese fin de semana, comenzaron a verse con mayor frecuencia en Estados Unidos. Fue el medio Star quien destapó las primeras alarmas en septiembre de 2025 al reportar citas discretas en Nueva York y Los Ángeles. Durante esos meses, el entorno de la actriz aseguraba que preferían tomarse las cosas con calma y mantener un perfil bajo, especialmente por el revuelo mediático debido a la diferencia de edad y la fama de Braun. Finalmente, la pareja decidió dejar de esconderse e hizo pública su relación asistiendo juntos a la premiere de la nueva temporada de ‘Euphoria’. Poco después, oficializaron su amor en redes sociales.
